## Load required packages
```{r load-packages, include false}
options("install.lock" = FALSE,
        "repos" = c(CRAN = "https://cloud.r-project.org")) # Replace with your target repo URL
if (!require("pacman")) install.packages("pacman") ; library(pacman)
pacman::p_load(
  rio,          # File import
  here,         # File locator
  skimr,        # get overview of data
  tidyverse,    # data management + ggplot2 graphics, 
  gtsummary,    # summary statistics and tests
  rstatix,      # statistics
  nortest,      # Anderson-Darling test for normality
  moments,      # skewness and kurtosis
  corrr,        # correlation analayis for numeric variables
  janitor,      # adding totals and percents to tables
  flextable,    # converting tables to HTML
  dplyr,        # For data manipulation
  ggplot2,      # For creating plots
  plotly,
  DescTools,    # For statistical functions like skewness and kurtosis
  car,          # For Levene's test and ANOVA
  vctrs,         # For data type handling
  rvest,
  tidyr,
  vars,
  httr,
  jsonlite,
  ISOweek,
  lubridate
            )
```

## Get data
```{r read-data, echo=FALSE}
# Define the API endpoint
api_endpoint <- "https://data.gov.il/api/3/action/datastore_search?resource_id=2de7b543-e13d-4e7e-b4c8-56071bc4d3c8&limit=400000"

# Send GET request to the API
response <- GET(api_endpoint)

# Check if the request was successful (status code 200)
if (status_code(response) == 200) {
      # Extract content as text and parse JSON
      content <- content(response, as = "text", encoding = "UTF-8")
      data <- fromJSON(content)
      records <- data$result$records    # Extract the records from the result
      df <- as.data.frame(records)      # Convert records to a data frame
      } else {
       cat("Error: Failed to fetch data. Status code:", status_code(response), "\n")
     }
glimpse(df)
```

## Clean data
```{r clen-data, include false}
# Fix data
df <- df %>%
  mutate(Survey_Date = as.Date(Survey_Date))
  

df_monthly <- df %>%
  # 2. Use update() to force the day component to the 15th
 mutate(Month_15 = floor_date(Survey_Date, unit = "month") + days(14)) %>%

  # 3. Group and calculate the average Kinneret level
  group_by(Month_15) %>%
  summarise(Kinneret_Level_Monthly_Avg = mean(Kinneret_Level, na.rm = TRUE)) %>%
  ungroup()

# View the new data frame
glimpse(df_monthly)
```

## plot the Kinneret level
```{r deaths, include false}
plot <- ggplot(df_monthly, aes(x = Month_15, y = Kinneret_Level_Monthly_Avg)) +
  geom_line(color = "steelblue", linewidth = 1) +
  #geom_point(color = "darkred", size = 2) +
  labs(
    title = "Kinneret level",
    x = "Date",
    y = "Level (sea level meters)"
  ) +
  # scale_y_log10() +  # Add logarithmic y-axis
  theme_minimal()
ggplotly(plot)
```


## Plot the Smoothed Kinneret Level
```{r plot-smoothed, echo=FALSE, warning=FALSE, message=FALSE}
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)
library(plotly)

# Set your smoothing window (1 = no smoothing, 3 = light, 12 = high smoothing)
month_lag_window <- 12  

df_monthly_smoothed <- df_monthly %>%
  arrange(Month_15) %>%
  mutate(
    # Step 1: Cumulatively add the monthly averages
    Cumulative_Sum = cumsum(Kinneret_Level_Monthly_Avg),
    
    # Step 2: Difference the data
    Raw_Window_Sum = Cumulative_Sum - lag(Cumulative_Sum, n = month_lag_window),
    
    # Step 3: Divide by window size to scale values back to standard sea-level meters
    Smoothed_Signal = Raw_Window_Sum / month_lag_window
  )
glimpse(df_monthly_smoothed)

# Build a clean, simple line plot
plot_smooth <- ggplot(df_monthly_smoothed, aes(x = Month_15, y = Smoothed_Signal)) +
  geom_line(color = "steelblue", linewidth = 1) +
  labs(
    title = paste0("Smoothed Kinneret Trend (", month_lag_window, "-Month Window Average)"),
    x = "Date",
    y = "Level (sea level meters)"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()

ggplotly(plot_smooth)
```
